Study data

Source: R/data.R
baysesp_data.Rd

Summarises a study in which K binary tests are performed on every subject and the disease status is ascertained by the reference standard only for the verified subjects (Begg and Greenes, 1983; Baker, 1995). The data are reduced, without loss of information, to the counts of verified diseased, verified healthy and unverified subjects for each of the J = 2^K response profiles.

Usage

baysesp_data(data, tests, verified, disease, counts = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame. By default one row per subject; with counts, one row per combination of test results, verification and disease status.

tests

Names of the columns with the test results.

verified

Name of the column that says whether the subject was verified.

disease

Name of the column with the disease status. It may be missing (NA) only for unverified subjects, and it is ignored for them.

counts

Optional name of a column with the number of subjects in each row, for data that are already aggregated.

Value

An object of class baysesp_data.

Details

Test results, verification and disease status must be coded as 0/1 or as logical values, with 1 (TRUE) meaning positive, verified and diseased.

The object has the properties @tests, @profiles (a J x K matrix of the response profiles, in binary order: the first row has all tests negative and the first test varies fastest), @n_diseased, @n_healthy and @n_unverified (counts for each profile) and the read-only @never_verified (profiles without any verified subject). as.data.frame() returns the aggregated table.

References

Baker, S. G. (1995). Evaluating multiple diagnostic tests with partial verification. Biometrics, 51(1), 330–337. doi:10.2307/2533339

Begg, C. B. and Greenes, R. A. (1983). Assessment of diagnostic tests when disease verification is subject to selection bias. Biometrics, 39(1), 207–215. doi:10.2307/2530820

Examples

d <- simulate_study(n = 1000, prevalence = 0.1,
                    sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8),
                    specificity = c(A = 0.95, B = 0.9),
                    verification_prob = c(0.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1))
baysesp_data(d, tests = c("A", "B"), verified = "verified", disease = "disease")
#> <baysesp_data> 2 tests, 4 profiles, 1000 subjects, 291 verified
#> never-verified profiles: none
#> 
#>  A B diseased healthy unverified
#>  0 0        0      88        683
#>  1 0       14      30         12
#>  0 1        7      74         14
#>  1 1       72       6          0

# aggregated data
agg <- data.frame(T1 = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1),
                  V  = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0),
                  D  = c(0, 0, 1, 1, NA, NA),
                  n  = c(40, 5, 2, 30, 300, 20))
baysesp_data(agg, tests = "T1", verified = "V", disease = "D", counts = "n")
#> <baysesp_data> 1 test, 2 profiles, 397 subjects, 77 verified
#> never-verified profiles: none
#> 
#>  T1 diseased healthy unverified
#>   0        2      40        300
#>   1       30       5         20
